findings.message: The `turn` helper's `opts` parameter declares optional properties without the explicit `| undefined` (`result?: 'pass' | 'fail'`, `judge?: () => unknown`, `runner?: (...) => Promise<ValidationCheckResults>`). The same file's `runImplementThenValidate` follows the rule (`summary?: string | undefined`), as do `runTurn` and `action` in chat-panel.ts. Test-helper scope only; whether this line was introduced by this Story was not confirmed.

The `readTests` return type declares optional properties without the explicit `| undefined` (`commit?: string`, `reported?: unknown`). Test-helper scope only; whether this line was introduced by this Story was not confirmed.
The `editPrompts` return type declares `review?: boolean` without the explicit `| undefined`. Test-helper scope only; whether this line was introduced by this Story was not confirmed.

The `toolCall` return type declares optional properties without the explicit `| undefined` (`command?: string`, `mcp?: unknown`); `toolResult` at line 449 does the same (`command?: string`, `exitCode?: number`). Test-helper scope only; whether these lines were introduced by this Story was not confirmed.

Grounding caveat, not a coverage gap: the graph's testsReaching edges are empty for every production symbol in the changed set (approval-queue.ts, chat-panel.ts, cli-adapter.ts, render-registry.ts, validation-checks.ts) because the tests are anonymous top-level test() callbacks the graph does not link. No HIGH was raised from that hollow grounding; coverage was judged by running the suites instead. The four changed plugin test files ran 269 tests, 269 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; the two changed build-step test files ran 87 tests, 87 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. 20 of the 21 promised tests are present under their exact titles (3 in approval-queue.test.ts, 1 in cli-adapter.test.ts, 1 in render-registry.test.ts, 15 in chat-panel.test.ts) and pass. The 21st, 'single request: the existing approve/deny/exact-command/tool-name/dir-block/suppressEcho tests keep passing unchanged', is not a test of its own; the existing single-request tests in chat-panel.test.ts (dir-block approve, deny, in-turn relay, suppressEcho, outcome row) are present and pass, but whether they are textually unchanged was not checked. No build record was supplied, so the pass-state rests on this local run only.
